food_roles.title: Sunrise, midday and the later offering
food_roles.text: Joshi places khichdi and ghadghadia tarkari at sunrise, with an individual offering in each family member’s name. His midday account brings prepared foods to the tulasi platform and includes a Samba Dashami Brata Katha reading. A later Mahakala Puja has Budha Chakuli offered to Yama. Keeping these acts separate prevents a Surya offering list from becoming a single menu for every part of the day.

food_roles.title: Named foods and the sharing that follows
food_roles.text: The essay names manda, kakara and arisha pithas, Makar Chaula, Chhenaguda, khiri, rasagola, chhenagaja and sweet curd among foods prepared through the day. It describes dishes first offered to Surya and later shared with children. This is a source-specific food list, not a required household menu, tested recipe or current visitor meal. The companion preparation pages describe food forms; they do not verify this ritual’s local ingredients or quantities.

food_roles.title: A printed ambiguity to preserve
food_roles.text: The midday passage prints “beetle” in its description of the turmeric-water bowl. The page image confirms that spelling. Its intended object remains unresolved: we do not silently substitute betel, a leaf or another item. An Odia katha, another edition or a situated household account is needed before using that detail as a ritual instruction.
